newsitem.title: INDIA: Rail link to boost India-CIS trade ties - industry.
newsitem.headline: Rail link to boost India-CIS trade ties - industry.

text.p: India's bilateral trade with the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) would rise to $5 billion by 2000 with completion of a missing rail link in Iran, a leading trade association said on Monday.
The Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry (ASSOCHAM) said the new rail route links Bandar Abbas and Tazarge, and Mashad and Srakha, quickening trade.
ASSOCHAM is organising a two-day meeting on trade with CIS countries from Tuesday.

"India's trade with CIS is expected to increase significantly, touching the $5 billion mark by the end of the century from $2 billion at present with the completion now of the missing rail link in Iran," ASSOCHAM said in a statement.
It said with these links it was possible to organise all-rail movement of both containerised and bulk traffic from Bandar Abbas to all the important points in the Central Asian Republics.
The most feasible route to the central Asian Republics is the sea route from Bombay to Bandar Abbas in Iran and further by rail or road into the Central Asian Republics.
"The new route is not only shorter but also cheaper and less time-consuming," it added.
India's trade with the former Soviet republics fell almost 88 percent in 1992/93 (April-March) from levels in 1990/91, after the disintegration of the Soviet Union.
Bilateral trade in 1995/96 was put at 77.08 billion rupees.
The statement said the CIS countries were opting for Indian technology to set up small and medium scale industries to make consumer goods and consumer durables.

The core sectors identified for Indian participation in the CIS countries include fruits and vegetables, garments, detergents, cosmetics, computer software, consumer electronics, light engineering products and textiles.
